rationale.conceptual: Requires careful implementation of DFT with virtual crystal approximation, convergence of k-points for transport, and use of BoltzTrap with rigid-band model. Not a trivial single-command operation, but the methods are well-established.
rationale.execution: 3-stage pipeline: two DFT calculations (one with virtual crystal) then BoltzTrap transport. Requires handling external codes, file I/O, and proper convergence. Dependencies are straightforward but need careful orchestration.

difficulty.reasoning: The task involves reproducing Seebeck coefficients using standard DFT (LDA) and Boltzmann transport (BoltzTrap). The conceptual difficulty is moderate: DFT setup with virtual crystal approximation, k-point convergence, and transport integrals require understanding of solid-state physics and computational tools. Execution is a multi-step pipeline of two DFT runs and one transport step, with external tooling but not overly complex. Resource needs are modest: two DFT runs on a dense k-mesh (CPU only), small data.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Two DFT band structure calculations on dense k-meshes (~11,000 points) dominate; each run may need ~16 GB RAM for wavefunctions and eigenvalues. Input structures are tiny (<1 MB), so data is negligible.
